recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-18550 unless a future work group decision revisits GET/POST search conformance or logging guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-18550 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and requested more guidance in the HTTP search section warning that required GET and POST search support can expose sensitive search parameters and PHI in request parameters and client/server logs; the resolution was to repeat the warning as requested.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by commit 06e4aba5d2d49c420d28c6cc77b35484baa9830b, which added a note to source/http.html saying PHI can appear in search parameters and HTTP logs, logs should be treated as sensitive as the resources, and the security page has further commentary.
additional_context: Later same-section work changed the surrounding conformance text. FHIR-31943 revised GET/POST search support expectations and added explicit nuance that neither GET nor POST is inherently more secure and implementers must verify logging protection. FHIR-39137 moved search protocol content into source/http.html while preserving and broadening the FHIR-18550 note. Negative Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/http.html currently warns about PHI in request query parameters and HTTP logs, states that logging processes must protect PHI and other sensitive data, and preserves the note that logs should be treated as sensitive as the resources themselves.
